matched_bugs: task_counter is read and incremented without any lock, so two concurrent submit() calls can get the same task_id, with the second overwriting the first's TaskResult in self.results.

The shutdown_flag check and task enqueue are not atomic â€” a thread can pass the shutdown check, then shutdown() is called, then the task is enqueued into a pool that is shutting down, potentially losing the task.
Setting shutdown_flag causes workers to exit their loop even if there are tasks remaining in task_queue, silently dropping pending tasks.
TaskResult.get() busy-waits in a tight loop ('while not self.done: pass') which wastes CPU and, due to Python's GIL, may actually slow down the worker thread that is trying to set done=True.
get_completed_count iterates over self.results.values() without any lock while submit() concurrently modifies self.results, which can cause RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration.
